entries.title: Event, data, and event-data ports
entries.applicability: A requirement specifies an event notification, sampled data, or an event carrying typed data.
entries.explanation: Preserve all three decisions independently: direction (in/out/in out), port kind (event/data/event data), and any required data classifier. An event port carries no data classifier; a data or event data port can name a data classifier. Write 'data port Reading', never 'data port type Reading'. Do not simplify a required event data port into an event port just because both parse. Static validity does not establish requirement coverage.

entries.title: Component types and implementations
entries.applicability: Declaring a component interface and its implementation, or selecting a subcomponent classifier.
entries.explanation: A component type declares its features; an implementation names its own type followed by a dot and an implementation suffix. The category and end name must match. Do not replace a required system with a device to avoid a modeling difficulty. A subcomponent may legally use an appropriate type classifier; when the requirement asks for an implementation or a concrete instance hierarchy, provide the requested implementation rather than silently dropping it.

entries.title: Connect two sibling system subcomponents
entries.applicability: A parent system contains sibling systems whose ports communicate.
entries.explanation: The parent's implementation owns subcomponent declarations and their connection. A source out port on one child can connect to a destination in port on the other child. Use child-name.feature-name for both endpoints. Types are declared at package scope; their containment hierarchy is expressed through implementation subcomponents, not by nesting type declarations textually. Keep the categories and connection directions requested by the user.

entries.title: A local classifier may be defined later
entries.applicability: A subcomponent references a classifier whose declaration occurs later in the same package.
entries.explanation: A missing declaration in a generation prefix is a pending obligation, not proof of an error. Later define the referenced type and implementation with the required category; append-only generation cannot repair an already established category conflict. End the complete project only after outstanding required definitions are resolved. Forward references do not justify inheritance or containment cycles, and example declarations are not available in the generated project.

entries.title: Data size, property units and precise quantities
entries.applicability: A requirement fixes the storage size of a data classifier.
entries.explanation: Attach Data_Size to the intended data classifier in its properties section, preserve the requested magnitude, and use units defined by the loaded property environment. The pinned AADL Size_Units defines KByte as 1000 Bytes; do not silently interpret it as 1024 Bytes. If the source requirement is ambiguous about decimal/binary units, record that evaluation ambiguity rather than declaring exact fulfillment. A well-typed size property alone does not specify record fields or prove end-to-end format consistency.

entries.title: Single-source output and model-unit closure
entries.applicability: Closing the single generated source, or diagnosing an extra package/model unit outside the configured output scope.
entries.explanation: The current generation scope is exactly one .aadl source file containing one package or one property set. Multiple model units are outside this output scope; do not add another file to bypass the limit. A single package may contain many component types and implementations, including legal references to declarations later in that same package. Close its AADL model unit before closing the file. END_FILE and END_PROJECT are transport control lines, not AADL source: do not prefix them with the source-line marker. All required local declarations must exist before project closure. This is the selected generation and OSATE profile, not a claim that AADL itself cannot express larger projects.

entries.title: Direction depends on connection context
entries.applicability: Checking connections between a parent boundary and a child, or diagnosing source/destination direction errors.
entries.explanation: A child source endpoint is normally out (or in out); a child destination is in (or in out). At the containing component boundary, an incoming parent port can be the source of an internal connection to a child's input, and a child's output can connect to an outgoing parent port. Do not apply the child-source-out rule to the parent boundary. Resolve endpoint ownership and features before checking both-end compatibility; defer information that genuinely requires later definitions.

entries.title: Names, scope and end-name matching
entries.applicability: A diagnostic concerns duplicate members, mismatched end names or invisible declarations.
entries.explanation: AADL names are case-insensitive. A completed duplicate member name in the same relevant scope is a conflict; differently scoped members may share a name. Do not reject an unfinished identifier merely because its current spelling matches a declared name: it may still be extended. Match the package/type/implementation end name with its opening name. Keep declarations in their intended public/private section. Retrieval does not change declaration visibility or define a missing classifier.
